GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.title: Gorgias: The Sealed Crate
A sealed crate bears the label “grain”. No one has inspected its contents. Gorgias asks what speech can make a crowd do, and what it cannot establish. This uses your remaining question.
Spend this act’s question on one public claim.
Spend the question without testing this claim.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.SPEECH.desc: People await a grain delivery. You know only the label and unbroken seal. What will you tell them?
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.SPEECH.opti: “The grain is here. Distribute it now.”
Gain quick agreement while claiming an unverified fact.
“The label says grain. Open it first.”
Keep the evidence boundary; distribution waits.
Spend the question without making a claim.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.STRONG_CLAI: The crowd agrees to distribute the crate at once. Your words changed their plan, but no one opened it. What does their agreement show?
Infer the contents from the crowd’s assent.
The speech moved them; the contents remain unknown.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.CAUTIOUS_CL: The crowd delays distribution and asks to open the crate. Your careful words changed their plan, but no one has opened it yet. What does the delay show?
Treat delay as proof of absence.
Infer an empty crate from the crowd’s caution.
The speech slowed them; the contents remain unknown.
You used the crowd’s reaction as evidence about the crate. Agreement does not put grain inside; delay does not remove it. The label and seal still need inspection.
Keep this question without changing your route.
Leave this speech without a new route claim.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.BELIEF_ONLY: You distinguish a change in belief from knowledge of the contents. Speech can move action before inspection; whether grain is inside remains open.
Keep this question without changing your route.
Leave this speech without a new route claim.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_RECO: You record a limited question about persuasion and knowledge. Aristotle remains your current route; the tablet and combat practice remain.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_KEPT: You keep the category practice without a new account. This act’s question is spent; your route and relic remain.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_STOP: You stop before making a claim. The question is spent; your current route remains.
GORGIAS_SPEECH_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_DECL: You decline the inquiry. The question is spent; your current route remains.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.title: Anaxagoras: Order in the Mixture
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.INVITAT: You kept Parmenides rather than adopting the atomist account. Anaxagoras asks whether an already mixed world can change without anything coming from nothing. This uses your remaining question.
Spend this question to test a parallel explanation.
Spend this question and keep Parmenides.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.MIXTURE: Imagine a mixture in which one visible color dominates. Will you explain the appearance by its greater share, or demand a completely pure portion? The visible example cannot prove that every ingredient is everywhere.
Keep unseen shares possible without claiming to have observed them.
Test what a claim of universal mixture would forbid.
Leave the account untested and spend this question.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.PREDOMI: A greater share can explain why this color appears, but cannot prove that every possible ingredient was present. What explanatory role will you demand of Mind?
Leave local arrangements to further material explanation.
Require an account of every result.
Ask why each arrangement is the best one.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.PURE_DE: If every portion still contains every ingredient, a completely pure piece cannot be drawn from this model. That is a theoretical burden, not a result established by these colors. What will Mind explain?
Leave local arrangements to further material explanation.
Require an account of every result.
Ask why each arrangement is the best one.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.MIND_ST: You limit Mind to starting the motion that separates the mixture. Later local arrangements still need an account; the start alone does not explain why each one is best.
Keep the mixture and Mind as an open comparison, not a new route.
Do not record a new explanatory account.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.MIND_EV: You demand that Mind explain why each particular arrangement is best. Plato later criticizes this promise as unfulfilled; do not put that criticism in Anaxagoras’s own mouth.
Keep the mixture and Mind as an open comparison, not a new route.
Do not record a new explanatory account.
ANAXAGORAS_MIXTURE_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_: You record a limited question about mixture and Mind. Parmenides remains your current route. No graph turn, relic, or combat reward follows.
You keep Parmenides without recording a new account. This act’s question is spent; the current route and relic remain.
You stop before settling the explanation. The question is spent; Parmenides remains.
You decline the inquiry. The question is spent; Parmenides remains.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.title: Empedocles: Four Roots in Relation
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.INVITATIO: A second account of change follows the atomist decision. Empedocles keeps four roots from arising or vanishing, then asks what union and separation explain. Compare it without leaving your atomist route.
Use this act’s question to examine a parallel model.
Spend this question without a new comparison.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.BURDEN.de: Which change needs explaining? Choose one burden; the other remains untested. Love and Strife name ways of joining and separating, not moral rewards.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.BURDEN.op: Ask how unchanged roots can form different things.
Ask how an existing mixture can come apart.
Keep the question unresolved and spend this opportunity.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.COMPOSITI: Imagine one portion each of earth, water, air, and fire. Do you mix these unchanged roots or leave each kind apart?
A combination can differ without any root being born.
The model remains sorted; it explains no mixed thing yet.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.SEPARATIO: Begin with one portion each of earth, water, air, and fire mixed together. Do you sort like with like or preserve the mixture?
Separation changes the arrangement, not the inventory.
No separation is shown; the current structure depends on continued joining.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.MIXED.des: Unlike roots now form one arrangement. A change of proportion could yield another, but the model does not prove that Love alone makes the world.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.MIXED.opt: Mark the parallel account while keeping Democritus as your current route.
Do not add the Empedocles comparison.
The roots remain distinct. Their persistence does not by itself explain a mixed creature or settle the cosmic cycle.
Mark the parallel account while keeping Democritus as your current route.
Do not add the Empedocles comparison.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.SORTED.de: The mixture is sorted without any root appearing from nothing. This illustrates separation, not a proof that Strife is evil.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.SORTED.op: Mark the parallel account while keeping Democritus as your current route.
Do not add the Empedocles comparison.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.HELD.desc: The mixture remains. Its stable appearance does not show what would happen under stronger separation.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.HELD.opti: Mark the parallel account while keeping Democritus as your current route.
Do not add the Empedocles comparison.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_RE: You record a limited comparison with Empedocles. The four-root model offers another answer to the Eleatic challenge; your Democritus route and Lyre and Bow remain. No combat reward.
Close this question without another reward.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_KE: You keep the atomist account without adding this comparison. The second-act question is spent; no reward or route change.
Close this question without another reward.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_ST: You stop before making a comparison. The question is spent, and the atomist route remains.
Close this question without another reward.
EMPEDOCLES_ROOTS_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_DE: You decline the parallel inquiry. The question is spent; your current route remains.
Close this question without another reward.

DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.title: Democritus: Void and Arrangement
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.options.RECOVERIN: Choices are locked. If recovery stops, retain the evidence and reload this run.
Leucippus and Democritus explain change through unchanging units and void. Choose one question to examine with a thought model.
Decide what this account will explain.
Decline the inquiry and resolve this act's fixed invitation.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.INQUIRY.des: What will this account examine: how units move, or how the same units yield different appearances? Your question and operation will be recorded.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.INQUIRY.opt: Record the conditions for units to change places.
Record how composition and sensation relate.
Keep your choices and resolve this act's fixed invitation.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.MOTION_MODE: This model only permits units to move one at a time into a vacancy. It does not represent every kind of motion. Keep the shapes and number fixed: will you leave a vacancy or fill every place?
Allow a vacancy in the model without yet asserting real void.
Keep the no-void premise and the gap in explaining motion.
Keep your choices and resolve this act's fixed invitation.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.QUALITY_MOD: The same hooked model pieces feel rough along their outward hooks. Turn the hooks inward, or keep the arrangement and touch it from another side. These pieces are not atoms.
Turn the hooks inward, making the outer edge smooth.
Keep the arrangement and touch the same pieces from another side.
Keep your choices and resolve this act's fixed invitation.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.VACANT_MOTI: The units change places without coming from nothing. The vacancy permits motion in this model; it does not prove real void exists. Will you accept atoms and void?
Turn to Democritus while retaining the comparison's limits.
Retain the comparison without adopting atoms and void.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.PACKED_MOTI: With these stepwise rules, a packed model cannot move a unit. This does not rule out collective motion in other models. You keep the no-void premise and still owe an account of motion.
Turn to Democritus while retaining the comparison's limits.
Retain the comparison without adopting atoms and void.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.REARRANGED_: The same hooks turn inward, leaving a smooth outer edge. The pieces keep their shapes. Composition explains a difference in this model; it neither establishes real atoms nor excludes other explanations.
Turn to Democritus while retaining the comparison's limits.
Retain the comparison without adopting atoms and void.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.CHANGED_OBS: The hooks still face outward. A rough side and a smooth face feel different, while the arrangement stays fixed. Changed contact does not establish rearranged units; sensation still starts the inquiry.
Turn to Democritus while retaining the comparison's limits.
Retain the comparison without adopting atoms and void.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.RESULT_ADOP: You accept unchanging atoms and void, explaining change through composition and position. Your comparison and its limits remain recorded. The route turns to Democritus; the lyre remains your tool.
End this event without changing combat abilities.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.RESULT_KEPT: You retain the operation and its limits without concluding that reality consists of atoms and void. You remain with Parmenides; this act's fixed invitation is resolved.
End this event without changing combat abilities.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.RESULT_STOP: The inquiry stops with the choices already made. You have not adopted atomism. Your route and lyre remain; this act's fixed invitation is resolved.
End this event without changing combat abilities.
DEMOCRITUS_ARRANGEMENT.pages.RESULT_DECL: You decline the model inquiry, keeping Parmenides and the lyre. This act will not repeat the fixed invitation.
End this event without changing combat abilities.
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.title: Whose Turn to Hold the Seal
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.pages.INVITATION: On the second-act road, a public repair has two registered decision-makers: you today, your companion tomorrow, then you again. The craftworker supplying the repair is outside the roll and may only carry it out. Aristotle raises questions of community and citizenship.
Publish a rule, then face the response.
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.pages.ARRANGEMEN: Publish an arrangement before anyone agrees to it. You can concentrate the seal in your own hands or retain rotation between the two registered members. The craftworker remains outside that roll. This inquiry grants no resources or combat powers.
Claim sole control, without claiming agreement.
Your companion acts tomorrow; the craftworker is still excluded.
Keep your choices as unfinished and close this fixed opportunity.
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.pages.CENTRAL_CH: Your companion refuses to present his repair judgment as your command. He will not sign jointly. You can share the decision and let him reject your proposal, or rule alone without claiming his judgment and support.
Allow your companion to reject your proposal.
Accept that the other person does not join the judgment.
Keep your choices as unfinished and close this fixed opportunity.
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.pages.ROTATION_C: Your companion accepts the turn tomorrow. The craftworker asks why bearing the work gives no part in its decision. Giving them the following turn costs your own next turn; retaining the original roll keeps them outside.
Give my next turn to the craftworker.
Your companion acts tomorrow; you surrender the following turn.
Retain your turn and exclude the craftworker.
Keep your choices as unfinished and close this fixed opportunity.
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.pages.SHARED_DEC: You share the decision. Your companion participates on his own judgment and may reject your proposal. You have lost unilateral control; no outcome has been certified as correct.
Adopt the route without rewards or erasing your consequences.
Close this transition; your arrangement remains.
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.pages.KEPT_CONTR: You keep sole control. Your companion neither signs jointly nor lends his judgment to your decision. Authority remains yours; a common judgment has not occurred. Concentration does not guarantee a better repair.
Adopt the route without rewards or erasing your consequences.
Close this transition; your arrangement remains.
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.pages.EXTENDED_T: The craftworker takes the turn after your companion; you surrender your own next turn. The intervening turn stays with your companion. Participation expands without creating extra turns or eliminating disagreement.
Adopt the route without rewards or erasing your consequences.
Close this transition; your arrangement remains.
You retain your next turn. The craftworker still bears the repair work but has no part in its decision. Rotation holds within the roll; that does not make everyone affected a participant.
Adopt the route without rewards or erasing your consequences.
Close this transition; your arrangement remains.
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_ADO: You continue by asking how different roles share a community and who counts as a citizen. The route turns to Aristotle. The concessions or exclusions you chose remain; his name does not justify them. The Civic Seal remains your existing combat tool.
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_KEP: You retain the Plato route and close this fixed transition. Your arrangement is not undone, and its unresolved membership question remains.
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_STO: The inquiry stops here. Your published arrangement remains unfinished; no agreement, expanded participation or adoption is invented. This second-act fixed opportunity closes.
ARISTOTLE_CIVIC_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_DEC: You decline the arrangement and do not adopt Aristotle. This second-act fixed opportunity closes; your current route remains.
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.title: The Unsayable Source
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.pages.INVITATION.desc: A bronze cup can be recast. Parmenides' poem asks a prior question: where does what comes to be come from? If from what is not, what source have you named? If it already is, why call it coming to be?
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.pages.INVITATION.opti: Examine an account of coming to be.
Fix a subject, then face the limits of the argument.
No change of position; this invitation is consumed.
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.pages.REFERENT.descri: Fix what your account is about: What Is itself, or this particular cup? Your next reason must address that same subject. Cup, bronze and What Is cannot silently replace one another.
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.pages.REFERENT.option: A change in one artifact cannot stand in for the whole question.
Persistent material is not already a cup.
Keep the choices made; no adoption and no completed answer.
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.pages.WHOLE_CHALLENGE: Your subject is What Is itself. A source in what is not invokes the excluded path; a source in what is has not explained its previous absence. Withdraw the claim of coming to be, or contest this restriction?
Withdraw the claim and accept the boundary.
Turn toward Parmenides; keep the Lyre and Bow without another combat benefit.
Keep change and the unanswered challenge.
Remain with Heraclitus without claiming a refutation.
Keep the choices made; no adoption and no completed answer.
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.pages.CUP_CHALLENGE.d: Your subject is this cup. Saying bronze persists preserves the material, but the cup was not yet formed. Distinguish not being a cup from absolute non-being, or stop using the recast cup to establish coming to be?
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.pages.CUP_CHALLENGE.o: Not a cup does not mean nothing.
Keep the account of form, then face its limited scope.
Withdraw the claim and accept the boundary.
Turn toward Parmenides; keep the Lyre and Bow without another combat benefit.
Keep the choices made; no adoption and no completed answer.
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.pages.BOUNDARY.descri: Not being a cup is not absolute nothingness. This describes a change of form without explaining the coming to be of What Is itself. Keep that limited account, or accept a path that excludes non-being as a source.
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.pages.BOUNDARY.option: Keep change and the unanswered challenge.
Remain with Heraclitus without claiming a refutation.
Withdraw the claim and accept the boundary.
Turn toward Parmenides; keep the Lyre and Bow without another combat benefit.
Keep the choices made; no adoption and no completed answer.
You withdraw the truth claim of coming to be and turn toward Parmenides. Your argument no longer invokes non-being as a source; recasting may still be described as it appears. The Lyre and Bow remains, without an additional combat benefit.
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_KEPT.des: You keep your judgment of change and the question it faces. Recasting a cup is not the generation of What Is from nothing; observation alone has not answered the argument. Your inquiry remains with Heraclitus.
You stop the argument. Your chosen subject and unanswered question remain in its record. You have neither adopted a new position nor completed an answer by stopping.
PARMENIDES_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_DECLINED: You decline this inquiry. The Lyre and Bow remains and the map continues unchanged. Leaving will not renew this invitation.
Return to this run's three thinkers.
Return to the unified invitations without rerolling them.
Decline all invitations.
Continue without a philosophy relic.
Listen to Heraclitus.
Opposing pulls sustain the bow and lyre. Hear a question of being and change, and examine the practice.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_HERACLIT: Opposing pulls sustain the same bow. Heraclitus asks you to notice a common measure in change: keep a newly drawn card, use it directly, or play the opposite type first and spend it for a new card. The battle still leaves you to judge when to let go.
Listen to Socrates.
A game entry, not a claim of historical origin. Examine its question and practice.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_SOCRATES: Choose a question to pursue: how to examine knowledge, or how to examine conduct. One choice establishes one practice.
Listen to Plato.
A game entry, not a claim of historical origin. Examine its question and practice.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_PLATO.de: Listen to Plato here through the questions of forms and education. How can different functions sustain a common order? Establish a rule through action, then bear its inconvenience yourself.
Listen to Descartes.
A game entry, not a claim of historical origin. Examine its question and practice.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_DESCARTE: The revival of ancient skepticism, scholastic questions, and Montaigne form a background; Elisabeth's correspondence questions mind and body. Choose a particular enemy and let its visible intent alter your response.
Listen to Aristotle.
A game entry, not a claim of historical origin. Examine its question and practice.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_ARISTOTL: Aristotle develops systematic disagreements after Plato; later readers reinterpret him through commentaries and translation networks. Form a category from current cost and let classification alter later choices.
Listen to Rousseau.
A game entry, not a claim of historical origin. Examine its question and practice.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_ROUSSEAU: Hobbes, Locke, republican traditions, and natural law already pose questions of political order. Rousseau reopens civilization and common legislation; Wollstonecraft challenges his gendered education. Repetition forms convention; its convenience also strengthens your enemies.
Being and Change：Lyre and Bow
Retain the first eligible card drawn at turn start. Play the opposite type first, then play it to Exhaust it and draw 1.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_BEING_AN: You take the Lyre and Bow. Each turn, judge what to keep and what to let flow through attack and defense.
Knowledge and Doubt：Question Cup
At combat start, put up to 2 cards on the bottom of your draw pile, then draw that many.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_KNOWLEDG: You take the Question Cup and begin a practice of Knowledge and Doubt.
Virtue and Happiness：Reflective Weight
At combat start, choose an Attack or Skill to Retain and discount as it waits. It Exhausts when played.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_VIRTUE_A: You take the Reflective Weight and begin a practice of Virtue and Happiness.
Freedom and Institutions：Civic Seal
Your first Attack or Skill sets the law. Each turn, the first matching card costs 1 less and the first opposing card costs 1 more.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_FREEDOM_: You take the Civic Seal and begin a practice of Freedom and Institutions.
Self and Other：Meditation Lens
Your first single-target Attack marks an enemy. Later, its intent discounts a Skill or an Attack targeting it.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_SELF_AND: You take the Meditation Lens and begin a practice of Self and Other.
Language and Meaning：Category Tablet
Your first non-X card sets a current-cost category. The next 2 cards in that category cost 1 less.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_LANGUAGE: You take the Category Tablet and begin a practice of Language and Meaning.
History and Power：Uncarved Stone
The uniquely most-repeated card becomes convention. Using it next turn costs 1 less, but all enemies gain 1 Strength.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.WESTERN_HISTORY_: You take the Uncarved Stone and begin a practice of History and Power.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.title: The Philosophers' Gaze
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.INITIAL.descript: Beyond Neow's threshold, three thinkers from different traditions wait on the road ahead. Listen to one, or decline every invitation.
See how benevolence and ritual become action.
See how impartial care and opposition to aggression measure results.
See how non-action and softness follow the situation.
Pause before deciding to proceed alone.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.KONGZI_VIEWPOINT: Benevolence explains why one restrains oneself: others matter before action begins. Ritual explains how: each act takes its proper place. The Spire has little use for ceremony, but cares greatly about play order.
Establish order with a Skill or Power before attacking.
Gain Virtue by declining an available attack.
Take no relic and keep your own answer.
Impartial care includes others in the same reckoning, and mutual benefit judges the shared result. Opposition to aggression does not mean refusing defense; it means denying aggression its result. Mozi opens the slips: check the ledger first.
Share Block and build Mutual Benefit while nobody loses HP.
Stop a declared attack and gain Block next turn.
Take no relic and keep your own answer.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.LAOZI_VIEWPOINTS: Non-action is not idleness, but freedom from contrivance. Water is soft, yet yields around force and wears down what is hard. Laozi sets down slips and jade: leave something undone, and room remains for what follows.
Play sparingly, Retain your hand, and prepare the next turn.
Leave Energy unspent and soften incoming attacks.
Take no relic and keep your own answer.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.ACT_ONE_DECLINE_: Proceeding without the philosophers is also a choice. Will you end this encounter with a bow?
Take no Act One route relic.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.KONGZI_MUDUO.des: The bell sounds before the blade is drawn. You choose ritual before force, binding yourself to order first.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.KONGZI_QING_YU_P: Cool jade rests in your hand. You choose restraint when an attack was possible, storing Virtue. At least the reward system understood.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.MOZI_MO_SE_ZHU_J: The ink-dark slips place everyone on one ledger: shared Block, and Mutual Benefit only while nobody loses HP. Shared interests are hard to tally once someone flips the table.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.MOZI_SHOU_CHENG_: The diagram is yours. Opposing aggression is not standing still to be struck, but denying the attack its result. Secure this turn first; discuss peace under heaven later.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.LAOZI_WU_WEI_SHU: The slips remain unfinished, yet their meaning continues. You refrain from excess and leave both cards and strength for the next turn.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.LAOZI_SHUI_YU.de: The jade turns with the current. You keep strength in reserve and do not contend with force; when the blow falls, half its edge is gone.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.KONGZI_DECLINE.d: You thank Kongzi but take neither bell nor jade. The question remains, and the answer is still yours.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.MOZI_DECLINE.des: You thank Mozi but take neither slips nor diagram. The consequences have been weighed; the choice remains yours.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.LAOZI_DECLINE.de: You thank Laozi but take neither slips nor jade. Non-action needs no object, and the road follows its own course.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.DECLINE.descript: You bow and accept no teaching. The road ahead remains your own answer.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.CONTINUATION.des: Your earlier choice reaches the second Act. Benevolence, ritual, impartial care, opposition to aggression, non-action, and the preservation of life each have a successor. You may also keep the old teaching and its relic.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.CONTINUATION.opt: Ask how benevolent conduct becomes a righteous choice.
Build order through learning, standards, and practice.
Turn opposition to aggression into a practiced art of defense.
Distinguish sameness and difference within the unity of all things.
Let what went unused find another use.
Preserve yourself instead of being spent by external things.
Confirm before refusing a successor; your relic will not be replaced.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.MENGZI_VIEWPOINT: Mengzi advances from benevolence to righteousness: accumulated Virtue must become action when a choice is made. Bear Paw inherits the pendant's Virtue and turns it into Energy and draw at the start of combat.
Replace Green Jade Pendant and preserve all its Virtue.
Refuse Bear Paw; the pendant and its Virtue remain unchanged.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.XUNZI_VIEWPOINTS: Xunzi entrusts order to learning, standards, and repeated practice. Skill, Attack, Skill is not sudden inspiration, but a measure that can be tested.
Replace Muduo and practice the Skill, Attack, Skill measure.
Refuse Ink Line; Muduo remains unchanged.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.QIN_GULI_VIEWPOI: Qin Guli turns opposition to aggression into the craft of defending a city. Prepare against each declared assault; if none draws blood, its edge will be dulled on the following turn.
Prepare the defense: City Defense Machinery.
Replace City Defense Diagram, prepare Block for attacking enemies, and answer a successful defense with Weak.
Refuse City Defense Machinery; the diagram remains unchanged.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.HUISHI_VIEWPOINT: Mozi enters everyone in one account, but Hui Shi moves the counters: what is alike may still differ, and what differs may still be alike. All receive the same Block; only one who finds and breaks the boundary can turn that shared measure into momentum.
Unite sameness and difference: Enumeration Counters.
Replace Ink Bamboo Slips, grant shared Block, and reward the first enemy Block you break each turn.
Refuse Enumeration Counters; Ink Bamboo Slips remain unchanged.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.ZHUANGZI_VIEWPOI: Zhuangzi looks at the great gourd and sees not uselessness, but a use not yet found. Cards left by restraint may be played more lightly tomorrow and shelter you as they are used.
Replace Wu Wei Slips and turn restrained play into Retain, reduced costs, and Block.
Refuse the Great Gourd; Wu Wei Slips remain unchanged.
PHILOSOPHERS_GAZE.pages.YANGZHU_VIEWPOIN: Yang Zhu values a life not burdened by external things. Energy left unused may guard your life without being lost; after the blow passes, that strength returns to you.

ANAXIMANDER_ORIGIN_INQUIRY.title: Anaximander: The Unfixed Source
ANAXIMANDER_ORIGIN_INQUIRY.pages.INVITAT: Heat and cold, wet and dry all appear. If one visible quality is the source of everything, how does its contrary arise? Anaximander's surviving testimony poses this question without giving us a complete mechanism.
Use the second act's question; no combat reward is granted.
Keep your position and consume this invitation.
ANAXIMANDER_ORIGIN_INQUIRY.pages.OBSERVA: At a hypothetical shore, warmth dries a pool while a cold wind brings rain. Which visible quality, if any, deserves priority as the source?
Name one visible quality as first.
Test what this choice owes to its contrary.
Ask what an unfixed source explains and what remains unknown.
Leave the observed opposition without adopting an explanation.
ANAXIMANDER_ORIGIN_INQUIRY.pages.DETERMI: You name one visible quality as first. Its contrary still appears. Calling the first a source now owes an account of how the contrary can emerge.
Mark a limited revision, not proof of a new material or combat doctrine.
Remain with your present judgment without recording this revision.
ANAXIMANDER_ORIGIN_INQUIRY.pages.INDEFIN: You refuse to let any visible quality monopolize the source. The unfixed avoids favoring heat over cold, but this alone does not show how either comes to be.
Mark the explanatory demand without claiming a complete mechanism.
Do not take the unfixed source as an established answer.
ANAXIMANDER_ORIGIN_INQUIRY.pages.RESULT_: You record a limited challenge: no single visible contrary has earned priority as the source. This does not prove a complete account of separation. Your Heraclitus practice and Lyre and Bow remain, with no new combat reward.
Close the inquiry and retain this limited route record.
You keep the observed tension without adopting a proposed source. Your Heraclitus practice and Lyre and Bow remain. This question will not be offered again in this act.

ANAXIMENES_BREATH_INVITATION.title: Anaximenes: Breath in Motion
ANAXIMENES_BREATH_INVITATION.pages.INVIT: Air may become different visible things through rarefaction and condensation. Try carrying one unused Energy into another turn: a change of timing, not a new source of power.
Gain Breath in Motion. Ending a turn with Energy unspent grants 1 Energy and 1 card next turn.
Gain no relic. This invitation will not return.
ANAXIMENES_BREATH_INVITATION.pages.ACCEP: You take up Breath in Motion. Leave at least 1 Energy unspent at turn end to gain 1 Energy and draw 1 card next turn. Your Lyre and Bow remains in use.
Keep this practice for the rest of the run.
ANAXIMENES_BREATH_INVITATION.pages.DECLI: You keep your current rhythm and Lyre and Bow. This practice will not return in this run.
SENECA_DAILY_REVIEW.title: Seneca: Daily Review
SENECA_DAILY_REVIEW.pages.INVITATION.des: After Zeno, Seneca asks you to review one concrete habit, not to prove that your last assent was right. This review changes no route or reward.
SENECA_DAILY_REVIEW.pages.INVITATION.opt: Choose one recorded matter to inspect.
Close this one-time review without a conclusion.
SENECA_DAILY_REVIEW.pages.FOCUS.descript: One review can inspect one thing. Will you look at the judgment you left with Zeno, or at recorded times you could use help? The other remains unchecked.
Inspect the saved Zeno outcome; leave the aid record unchecked.
Inspect the earlier opening-choice record; leave the judgment unchecked.
SENECA_DAILY_REVIEW.pages.REVIEW_KEEP.de: Your saved Zeno outcome kept the statement. That records what you assented to; it does not show how you acted every day. Decide how to check it next time.
SENECA_DAILY_REVIEW.pages.REVIEW_KEEP.op: Return once before committing a way to check.
Record the limit of this one review.
Record a concrete intention for the next occasion, without claiming it happened.

SENECA_DAILY_REVIEW.pages.RESULT_JUDGMEN: You keep your way of checking a judgment while admitting that this review saw only a saved assent outcome. Your route and rewards stay as they were.
You resolve to compare the next judgment with a concrete action before repeating it. This is a recorded practice intention, not proof of a future act or a new doctrine.
SENECA_DAILY_REVIEW.pages.RESULT_AID_KEP: You keep your way of checking when you use help, without claiming that these few observations cover every choice. Your route and rewards stay as they were.

EPICTETUS_GUIDE_PRACTICE.title: Epictetus: The Guide and the Gate
EPICTETUS_GUIDE_PRACTICE.pages.INVITATIO: A fellow traveler asks you to guide them through an unstable gate. You can state the risk and offer a limited guide, promise safe passage, or decline the role. The gate and the traveler will not obey a promise.
Offer to lead as far as the known marker; do not guarantee the gate.
Begin guiding with an assurance you cannot fully guarantee.
Do not claim to have guided this traveler.
EPICTETUS_GUIDE_PRACTICE.pages.GATE_CLOS: You described the risk and began to guide. The gate closes before the traveler follows; they stay behind. The warning was your action, the closing gate and their decision were not yours. What will you do for the person you agreed to guide?
Return and guide by the detour.
Explain the changed route to this traveler and accompany them.
Warn later travelers first, then guide this traveler by the detour.

You promised safe passage and began to guide. The gate closes before the traveler follows; they stay behind and question your guarantee. Your promise was yours; the gate and their decision were not. What will you do for the person you agreed to guide?
Return and guide by the detour.
Explain the changed route to this traveler and accompany them.
Warn later travelers first, then guide this traveler by the detour.
EPICTETUS_GUIDE_PRACTICE.pages.RESULT_RE: You return, explain a known detour, and walk back with the traveler. You warned first and continued the guiding duty after the gate closed. Their eventual choice remains theirs; this is no proof that every judgment was right.
Close this practice without a reward or route change.

EPICTETUS_GUIDE_PRACTICE.pages.RESULT_PR: You return, acknowledge that your guarantee exceeded what you could ensure, explain a known detour, and walk back with the traveler. The earlier promise remains recorded; your second action does not erase it.
Close this practice without a reward or route change.

You mark the closed gate for later travelers, then return, correct your guarantee, and guide this person by a known detour. The mark and correction are your actions; the traveler’s trust is not yours to command.

MARCUS_AURELIUS_CAMP_PRACTICE.title: Marcus Aurelius: The Camp Duty
MARCUS_AURELIUS_CAMP_PRACTICE.pages.INVI: After a battle, you are temporarily helping restore passage through camp. A fellow traveler complains about the arrangement but has not said what is wrong. Your first reply can make the work more concrete, or you can decline this duty.
Ask what is needed, then state your duty.
Hear the concrete problem before describing the work you can take.
State your plan and invite correction.
Make your proposed arrangement public and ask what it misses.
Do not claim to have organized this camp work.
MARCUS_AURELIUS_CAMP_PRACTICE.pages.RESP: You ask what is needed, then explain the duty you can take. The western lamp is out; the traveler says they will not go there alone. The need and refusal are their report, not something your words could guarantee. What will you do?
Go together to repair the lamp.
Share the dark walk and repair with the traveler.
Mark the path and gather help.
Mark the darkness, invite another helper, then return to repair the lamp.

You state your proposed arrangement and invite a correction. The traveler points out that the western lamp is out and refuses to go there alone. Your plan needs a real response, not a demand for agreement. What will you do?
